c. 1348 BC (bridged): Suppiluliuma I makes Hayasa-Azzi a Hittite vassal. After he 'invaded Azzi-Hayasa and defeated its king, Karanni' near Kummaha he 'established it as a Hittite vassal state, drawing up a treaty with Hakkana'; the Suppiluliuma I page says 'This treaty was probably concluded early…
1315 BCE: Anniya revolts against Mursili II.
1312 BCE (counted): Mursili II reconquers Hayasa-Azzi in his tenth year, with 'formal submission' the following year.
1311 BCE (counted): Hayasa-Azzi submits to Mursili II.
c. 1200 BC: Hayasa-Azzi breaks up. 'After it broke up at the end of the 13th century BCE, former districts became independent city-states'; the page links this to Hatti's collapse around 1190 BCE.
c. 1200 BC: the confederation ends. The page names no successor: the districts become city-states and 'Azzi areas probably overlapped with Urartu's Nairi' (Assyrian records from about this time).

wars.name: Suppiluliuma I's war on Hayasa-Azzi
wars.outcome: Suppiluliuma I defeated Karanni near Kummaha and made Hayasa-Azzi a vassal by treaty with Hukkana, who married his sister; the treaty forced repatriation of captives and the cession of border territory.

wars.name: Mursili II's war on Anniya and Hayasa-Azzi
wars.outcome: Hittite victory at Ganuvara; Mursili II reconquered Hayasa-Azzi in year 10 and received its formal submission the following year.

certainty.note: The page lists many places but no frontier; the confederation's extent is approximate.
